manual_verification_result: PASSED - human in-app check, 2026-09-04. The reviewer re-seeded demo data (the seed is gated by the one-time localStorage flag `compass.migration.demo-data-seed-v2`, so their profile held a pre-`9eac7a10` seed with no attendee data at all - a plain reload could never fix it) and confirmed the badge renders and is visible on grid event cards. They explicitly confirmed walkthrough item 2 - the 1440-with-sidebar-open case - as working at their actual window size.
manual_verification_discrepancy_kept_on_: The human's in-app check is the accepted verdict, but it does NOT reproduce my automated measurement, and I am recording rather than discarding the disagreement. At exactly 1440x900 CSS px with the right sidebar open, Playwright measured the standup card at 130.1 x 23.7 and NO badge in the DOM (`[data-attendee-badge]` count 0 page-wide) - correct behaviour, since MIN_EVENT_WIDTH_FOR_ATTENDEE_BADGE is 140. The human observing badges at their real window means their effective column width exceeded 130px (larger monitor, browser zoom, OS scaling, or narrower sidebar). CONCLUSION: the 140 floor is real and does suppress the badge below ~140px card width; it simply does not bite at this user's actual layout. The follow-up 'decide whether to lower the 140 floor' therefore stays OPEN as a product question, not as a bug.

automated_browser_probe_by_reviewer.root_cause: The binding constraint at 1440-with-sidebar is MIN_EVENT_WIDTH_FOR_ATTENDEE_BADGE = 140 (the floor), NOT the 150 gate. The card is 23.7px tall, below MIN_EVENT_HEIGHT_FOR_TIME_LABEL = 36, so showTimeLabel is false and the 150 gate is never consulted. R-6's analysis reasoned about COLUMN width landing in the 140-170 band, but the code compares position.width, which is the CARD width and is narrower than its column. Lowering 170 -> 150 was a correct change to a constraint that does not bind in this scenario.
